quotes.text: We start from existing medical VQA datasets and curated clinical education resources

rationale: The paper names broad source categories and says images came from public academic datasets, but the main evidence does not give version/snapshot plus a task-to-source-record route. Later stray text mentions MIMIC-IV and patient identifiers, but this conflicts with the benchmark description and is not enough for full traceability.

quotes.text: All source assets are public and de-identified to the best of our knowledge.
Any institutional or ethics review requirements were handled according to local policy

rationale: Origin is public/de-identified clinical assets, collection is described through LMM drafting and clinician validation, and research-use/licence terms are reported. Ethics handling is also stated.

quotes.text: we compared the age, sex and race distribution of the benchmark patients against the U.S. adult inpatient population

rationale: The packet reports a comparison of age, sex, and race against a named target population. That meets the full representativeness anchor.

quotes.text: Safety testing identifies unsafe outputs like contraindicated medications; bias testing compares accuracy across different patient demographics.

rationale: The paper reports both unsafe-output testing and bias testing. No contradictory code evidence is provided.

quotes.text: We acknowledge that leakage of benchmark data into training sets is possible.

rationale: The benchmark acknowledges possible contamination and includes some indirect discussion, but does not report a developer-side control plus measured overlap/canary check. A limitation sentence alone would be 0; the hidden-label/run-time isolation evidence is scored more directly under C6/A9.

quotes.text: no network path from the agent sandbox, and they are not published in the repository

rationale: The paper states that the agent cannot reach ground-truth answers at run time and names mechanisms: separate evaluation service, no network path, and unpublished labels. This satisfies the full anchor.

quotes.text: Download the MedCTA dataset from the release file

rationale: The dataset is released/downloaded, and package recommendations are provided, but the evaluation uses live/deployed tools such as GoogleSearch and external API models. Software, judge models, and live services are not fully pinned with no dynamic external dependency.

quotes.text: Only trajectories that pass both technical and clinical review are included in MedCTA

rationale: The benchmark reports manually/clinician-verified executable reference trajectories, which is solvability evidence. It does not report a scripted oracle solution run through the grader.

searched: S1-S5. The benchmark tasks are tool-mediated clinical interpretation tasks using OCR, image description, search, and calculator tools, not tasks that change an environment state. The NA clause applies because no task changes environment state.

quotes.text: a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks

contradiction_quotes.text: a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks
A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: The paper reports an empirical random-agent success rate, which satisfies the full anchor. Code reports a different random-action rate, so the score is kept and a contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks

rationale: A do-nothing agent score is reported for all tasks in the cited statement. The task count differs from the main benchmark, but the item asks whether such a result is reported.

quotes.text: Aggregate clinical score | 0.62 | 0.60 | 13.5

rationale: The benchmark validates its automated clinical-reasoning judge against clinician audit results and reports agreement/error figures. This meets the full anchor.

quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7

contradiction_quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed

rationale: S1 reports repeated runs, separate random seeds, and a decoding temperature. Code states a conflicting temperature and seed policy, so the reported score is retained with a contradiction flag.

quotes.text: The bracketed interval is a normal-approximation 95% confidence interval

rationale: The packet reports confidence intervals for audit scores and discusses model comparisons, but does not show a CI/test for the headline model comparison. This supports partial credit.

quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7

contradiction_quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7
each task is run three times

rationale: S1 reports the number of runs per task, the seed/sampling policy, and independence. S4 reports a different run count and deterministic seed policy, so a contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks
where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead

rationale: The paper reports CIs, states the resampling unit as tasks, and addresses patient clustering by resampling patients when tasks share a patient. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs
agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs

rationale: The paper reports pass^8 and final environment-state agreement across eight reruns. That is action/state-level repeat-run reliability with a run count.

quotes.text: separate random seeds at temperature 0.7

rationale: Decoding parameters are reported, but exact provider snapshot IDs or release dates are not. OpenCompass/Lagent are named, but no harness commit/tag matching the reported results is provided.

quotes.text: exposed as a static tool schema via tool_meta

rationale: The benchmark defines tool schemas/static tool metadata and documents tool inputs/outputs. It does not document per-tool side effects or error/failure return semantics on reporting surfaces.

quotes.text: Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation.
Two tools consist of simulated stubs providing fixed placeholder responses.

rationale: S1 reports conformance testing and discloses simulated stubs. The packet does not show that the stub disclosure reaches S5, which is required for full credit when simulation exists.

searched: S1-S5. The benchmark tools are OCR, image description, region description, GoogleSearch, and Calculator, and no action is described as a clinical order, prescription, note, message, or state mutation. The NA clause applies.

quotes.text: Goal accuracy ( G_{\mathrm{acc}} ) measures final answer correctness
we use a structured LLM-as-judge framework with disentangled prompts

rationale: The grader inputs include final answers, executed trajectories, and LLM-as-judge assessment, and the paper gives a rationale for non-state grading. It does not report validation on labelled correct/incorrect state changes with per-class error rates on S1-S3.

quotes.text: no network path from the agent sandbox, and they are not published in the repository

rationale: The paper reports controls against answer-label leakage at run time, and says labels are not published in the repository. No canary or provenance marker on released tasks is reported.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family
per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: The benchmark reports slice results per task family and per patient subgroup by sex and race. It also states that slice tables include case counts.

quotes.text: real de-identified records from a hospital database
approved under a data use agreement
released under terms separate from the MIT code licence

rationale: The packet states that records are real de-identified hospital records, gives governance through a DUA and de-identification method, and states data terms separate from the code licence. All elements are present.
